Subject: High latency and 5xx spike impacting production (NimbleHealth)

Markus —

We started seeing a sharp rise in end-to-end latency across our production integration around 14:45 UTC. Error rates (5xx) for our key inference route spiked to ~18% and average p95 latency climbed from ~210ms to ~1.2s. This started right after our morning traffic push (promo traffic) and persists across multiple model variants.

Attached: nimble_latency_snapshot_20261008.png (screenshot of monitoring), and I attached the SLA we have on file for reference.

This is customer-facing traffic; our users are timing out. Can Redwood temporarily relax any quota/burst constraints or divert traffic to a lower-cost variant while you investigate? We need an ETA — this is P1 for us.

- Elenore
CTO, NimbleHealth

Immediate asks:
- Laura: please open a JIRA ticket (JIRA-OPS-8913) and request a temporary quota/burst lift for NimbleHealth, + ask routing to route a subset of traffic to the stable small-latency variant (model-small-latency-v2). We need a short-lived mitigation (30-90 minutes) while we root cause.
- Grace: run a quick check on model error rates and KV-cache hit % for their tenant keys (nimble-*). Share brief logs (top 10 failing endpoints).
- Neha: loop in capacity and billing — confirm if we can grant an emergency burst override for this account and note any downstream billing implications.

CCed the customer to keep them in the loop — I'll send a customer-facing note once we have the mitigation plan.

Regards,
Markus Klein

Laura/Team — results from the quick triage:
- Top level: model-large-ensemble shows increased tail latency and a higher retry rate under burst. Telemetry indicates the request fanout increased (our orchestration spun up more sub-requests per inference) which amplified backend load.
- KV cache drop explains higher load: misses lead to full compute paths. We saw a correlated increase in long-tail token generation for this customer (long prompts + open-ended completions).

Immediate mitigations applied (16:00 UTC):
- Temporary routing: 10% traffic -> model-small-latency-v2 (lower compute path).
- Emergency burst allowance (RB-2026-1147) submitted; infra acknowledged the request and applied a +30% burst window for nimble account. (Note: RB request may require executive approval if extended.)
- Short-term throttle tweak: we increased per-tenant concurrency cap by +2 to reduce queueing for their token-heavy routes.

Next steps (owner):
- Grace: continued monitoring for 30 mins, post-mortem prep.
- Laura: confirm with customer that mitigation is live and gather any meeting times they want.
- Neha: confirm billing path for an emergency extension past the initial 45 minutes.

I'll attach the initial logs to the JIRA ticket.

-Grace
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elenore — quick update and apologies for the impact.

What we did immediately:
- Applied an emergency burst allowance and increased per-tenant concurrency for NimbleHealth (initial 45-minute window).
- Shifted 10% of production traffic to a lower-latency model variant (model-small-latency-v2) as a canary.
- Infra & Reliability are monitoring closely; initial signs show error rate dropping to ~3% and p95 moving back toward ~260-320ms for the routed canary.

Next steps:
- We opened JIRA-OPS-8913 for a full root cause analysis; Grace will lead the post-mortem.
- If you want a short touchpoint with our infra team, Laura can coordinate a 30-minute bridge.
- We may need an executive sign-off if Nimble wants the emergency burst extended beyond the initial window; Laura and Neha are evaluating the billing/contract implications now.

We're treating this as top priority — I have escalated to our on-call exec if we need rapid extension. I will keep you updated every 30 minutes until stable.
